rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi treats the wording as glad tidings whose fulfillment shows the Prophet's truth: God would not announce through a messenger an unjust outcome or one that required falsehood about God.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الكلام خرج مخرج البشارة وليس يجوز أن يبشر الملك من قبل الله بالظلم والجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael's descendants had been confined to the desert and feared entering Iraq or Syria; Islam enabled them to spread east and west and mingle with nations.
rows.anchor: كانوا قبل الإسلام محصورين في البادية لا يتجاسرون على الدخول في أوائل العراق وأوائل الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet were false, the resulting contact between his people and other nations would be disobedience; God cannot give glad tidings of an outcome that is disobedience.
rows.anchor: فلو لم يكن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صادقا لكانت هذه المخالطة منهم للأمم ومن الأمم لهم معصية لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi cites Deuteronomy's promise of a prophet like Moses from the people's brothers as indicating a prophet outside Israel, just as an imam from the brothers of Banu Hashim would not be a Hashimite.
rows.anchor: إن الرب إلهكم يقيم لكم نبيا مثلي من بينكم ومن إخوانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob (Israel) had only Esau as a brother, and Esau's only prophetic descendant, Job, preceded Moses; prophets after Moses were Israelites, so the promised later prophet cannot be an Israelite.
rows.anchor: ثم إن يعقوب عليه السلام هو إسرائيل ولم يكن له أخ إلا العيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is the promised prophet from the brothers of Israel because Ishmael, his ancestor, was Isaac's brother.
rows.anchor: لكنه كان من إخوانهم لأنه من ولد إسماعيل الذي هو أخو إسحق

rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: An objection says the phrase from among you excludes Muhammad because he did not arise among the Israelites.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل قوله : ( من بينكم ) يمنع من أن يكون المراد محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that Muhammad arose among them geographically: he appeared in the Hijaz, was sent in Mecca, and migrated to Medina among nearby Jewish communities and near the Jews of Syria.
rows.anchor: بل قد قام من بينهم لأنه عليه السلام ظهر بالحجاز فبعث بمكة وهاجر إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase from among you also fits through kinship: since Muhammad was their brother by descent, his arising among them was not remote.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإنه إذا كان من إخوانهم فقد قام من بينهم فإنه ليس ببعيد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's third proof cites a passage saying God came from Sinai and appeared from Seir and Paran; Paran is in the Hijaz because the Torah says Ishmael practiced archery in Paran and he lived in Mecca.
rows.anchor: أن جبل فاران هو بالحجاز لأن في التوراة أن اسماعيل تعلم الرمي في برية فاران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage's grant of glory cannot refer to Ishmael, who gained no glory after settling there and was not surrounded by tens of thousands of saints; Razi therefore identifies the figure as Muhammad.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون المراد إسماعيل عليه السلام لأنه لم يحصل عقيب سكنى إسماعيل عليه السلام هناك عز

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: The Jews interpret the passage as fire appearing at Sinai, Seir, and Paran.
rows.anchor: قالت اليهود : المراد أن النار لما ظهرت من طور سيناء ظهرت من ساعير نار أيضا ومن جبل فاران أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the fire reading: God's coming from a place denotes an accompanying revelation, speech, punishment, or similar event, which the Jews acknowledge occurred only at Sinai.
rows.anchor: لو خلق نارا في موضع فإنه لا يقال جاء الله من ذلك إذا تابع ذلك الواقعة وحي نزل في ذلك الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited passage in Habakkuk supports the reading by saying God came from Sinai and the Holy One from Paran, then describing Muhammad and his community's triumph.
rows.anchor: جاء الله من طور سيناء والقدس من جبل فاران ، وانكشفت السماء من بهاء محمد

rows.speaker: ابن رزين الطبري
rows.claim: Ibn Razin al-Tabari transmits a version of the Paran prophecy that names Muhammad and depicts his armies, arrows, and deliverance of his nation and ancestral land.
rows.anchor: هكذا نقل عن ابن رزين الطبري .

rows.speaker: أبو الحسين
rows.claim: Abu al-Husayn says he saw Christian transmissions that explicitly name Muhammad al-Mahmud in the prophecy from Paran and speak of his people's salvation.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو الحسين رحمه الله في كتاب الغرر قد رأيت في نقولهم :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi concludes that the Torah's appearance of the Lord from Paran means the appearance of a person with these traits, namely Muhammad, rather than fire.
rows.anchor: فظهر بما ذكرنا أن قوله تعالى في التوراة : ( ظهر الرب من جبال فاران ) ليس معناه ظهور النار منه

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: An objection takes the passage to mean God's own coming because it ends by mentioning the rescue of the Messiah.
rows.anchor: فإن قالوا المراد مجيء الله تعالى ولهذا قال في آخر الكلام : ( وإنقاذ مسيحك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the figure cannot be God, since the passage describes riding horses, a radiant appearance, and crossing ancient mountains; Muhammad rescued Jesus from Jewish and Christian falsehoods.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز وصف الله تعالى بأنه يركب الخيول وبأن شعاع منظره مثل النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's fourth proof cites Isaiah's prophecy about a city identified as Mecca, to which nations and kings come and whose light attracts them.
rows.anchor: يريد مكة ، فقد دناوقتك وكرامة الله تعالى طالعة عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the prophecy's details fit Mecca: the armies of nations pilgrimage there and the sea's treasures flow toward it.
rows.anchor: فوجه الاستدلال أن هذه الصفات كلها موجودة لمكة فإنه قد حج إليها عساكر الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets the renewed praise for the house as Islam's replacement of the pre-Islamic talbiya, which admitted a partner, with the declaration that God has no partner.
rows.anchor: ثم صار في الإسلام : لبيك اللهم لبيك ، لا شريك لك لبيك ، فهذا هو الحمد الذي جدده الله لبيت محمدته

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: An objection says Isaiah's prophecy concerns Jerusalem and will be fulfilled in the future.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل المراد : بذلك بيت المقدس وسيكون ذلك فيما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi responds that it is incoherent to say the time is near if the event is distant, especially when the approaching event is displeasing; Isaiah's many references to the desert also disprove the Jerusalem reading.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يقول الحكيم : ( قد دنا وقتك ) مع أنه ما دنا بل الذي دنا أمر لا يوافق رضاه

rows.speaker: السمان
rows.claim: Al-Samman transmits from the Torah's first book God's promise to Abraham that Ishmael is answered, blessed, greatly increased, and will father twelve chiefs and a great nation.
rows.anchor: روى السمان في تفسيره في السفر الأول من التوراة أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi infers that Muhammad is the only descendant of Ishmael who became the leader of a great nation.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يكن في ولد إسماعيل من كان كان لأمة عظيمة غير نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham and Ishmael's prayer after building the Kaaba was for Muhammad, asking God to send a messenger from among them to recite revelation and teach and purify them.
rows.anchor: فأما دعاء إبراهيم عليه السلام وإسماعيل فكان لرسولنا عليه الصلاة والسلام لما فرغا من بناء الكعبة

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said he was Abraham's prayer and Jesus' glad tidings, linking the latter to Jesus' announcement of a messenger named Ahmad.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كان يقول عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( أنا دعوة أبي إبراهيم وبشارة عيسى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says Ahmad derives from praise, as do Muhammad and Mahmoud, and thus fits the Prophet in particular.
rows.anchor: فإنه مشتق من الحمد والاسم المشتق من الحمد ليس إلا لنبينا فإن اسمه محمد وأحمد ومحمود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says the Torah describes the Prophet as born in Mecca, residing in Tayba, ruling in Syria, and belonging to a community of praisers.
rows.anchor: قيل إن صفته في التوراة أن مولده بمكة ومسكنه بطيبة وملكه بالشام وأمته الحمادون

rows.speaker: المسيح
rows.claim: Jesus told the apostles that after he left, the Paraclete, the Spirit of truth, would come and speak only what he was told; Razi compares this with Muhammad's declarations that he follows revelation alone.
rows.anchor: قال المسيح للحواريين : ( أنا أذهب وسيأتيكم الفار قليط روح الحق الذي لا يتكلم من قبل نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi gives two readings of Paraclete: an accepted intercessor, a description of Muhammad, or, according to some Christians, one who distinguishes truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: أما ( الفارقليط ) ففي تفسيره وجهان : أحدهما أنه الشافع المشفع

rows.speaker: بعض النصارى
rows.claim: Some Christians explain Paraclete as the one who separates truth from falsehood, deriving it from Faruq and an intensive form; Razi says this too describes Islam's law.
rows.anchor: قال بعض النصارى : الفار قليط هو الذي يفرق بين الحق والباطل وكان في الأصل فاروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's seventh proof recounts Daniel's interpretation of a king's dream: successive metal kingdoms are struck by an uncut stone that becomes an everlasting kingdom filling the earth and abolishing the others.
rows.anchor: ويقيم إله السماء في تلك الأيام مملكة أبدية لا تتغير ولا تزول وإنها تزيل جميع الممالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi presents these passages from earlier scriptures as glad tidings of Muhammad's mission.
rows.anchor: فهذه هي البشارات الواردة في الكتب المتقدمة بمبعث رسولنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites say God's covenant is the rational obligation to give reward to the obedient, called a covenant because fulfillment is binding and stronger than an oath or vow.
rows.anchor: ذلك العهد هو ما دل العقل عليه من أن الله تعالى يجب عليه إيصال الثواب إلى المطيع

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's Ash'ari school denies that anything is owed by a servant upon God; since prior blessings ground the servant's duty, obedience does not generate a further duty of reward, contrary to the Mu'tazilites.
rows.anchor: وقال أصحابنا : إنه لا يجب للعبد على الله شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the proper account is that God's promised reward must occur: otherwise His truthful report would become a lie, which is impossible, making the promise more certain than an oath or vow.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنه تعالى لما وعد بالثواب وكل ما وعد به استحال أن لا يوجد ، لأنه لو لم يوجد لانقلب خبره الصدق كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, covenant means command: a servant may be commanded, while God cannot, and reciprocal wording is used similarly when God is called a deceiver or plotter.
rows.anchor: أن يقال العهد هو الأمر والعبد يجوز أن يكون مأمورا إلا أن الله تعالى لا يجوز أن يكون مأمورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi defines reverence or dread as fear, and the theologians define fear of God as fear of His punishment.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أن الرهبة هي الخوف قال المتكلمون : الخوف منه تعالى هو الخوف من عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may fear with certainty or with conjecture: one certain of having fulfilled every command and avoided every prohibition fears only what lies ahead.
rows.anchor: أما العلم فإذا كان على يقين من أنه أتى بكل ما أمر به واحترز عن كل ما نهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets and angels can be described as fearing God in this future-oriented sense.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا نصف الملائكة والأنبياء عليهم السلام بالخوف والرهبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When someone is unsure whether they obeyed fully or avoided prohibitions, fear arises from uncertainty about deserving reward.
rows.anchor: وأما الظن فإذا لم يقطع بأنه فعل المأمورات واحترز عن المنهيات فحينئذ يخاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the greater one's fear in this world, the greater one's safety on Judgment Day, and vice versa.
rows.anchor: أن كل من كان خوفه في الدنيا أشد كان أمنه يوم القيامة أكثر وبالعكس

rows.speaker: راوٍ غير مسمى
rows.claim: A report says God swears He will not combine two fears or two securities for a servant: the one secure from Him in this world will fear on Judgment Day, while the one who feared Him here will be secure then.
rows.anchor: ينادي مناد يوم القيامة وعزتي وجلالي إني لا أجمع على عبدي خوفين ولا أمنين

rows.speaker: العارفون
rows.claim: The gnostics distinguish fear of punishment, belonging to outward adherents, from fear of divine majesty, belonging to people of the heart; the first ends and the second never does.
rows.anchor: وقال العارفون : الخوف خوفان خوف العقاب وخوف الجلال ، والأول : نصيب أهل الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that abundant blessings make disobedience graver and that a covenant stated beforehand makes its breach more serious.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن في الآية دلالة على أن كثرة النعم تعظم المعصية ، ودلالة على ما تقدم العهد يعظم المخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage indicates that the Messenger was sent to Israelites as well as Arabs.
rows.anchor: ودلالة على أن الرسول كما كان مبعوثا إلى العرب كان مبعوثا إلى بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God alone extends also to hope and expectation, and Razi takes this exclusivity to support that all things occur by God's decree.
rows.anchor: وكما يجب ذلك في الخوف فكذا في الرجاء والأمل وذلك يدل على أن الكل بقضاء الله وقدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a servant acted independently, one would have to fear the servant as one fears God, and indeed fear oneself because control of reward and punishment would be in one's own hands; this would defeat the verse's exclusive command.
rows.anchor: لو كان العبد مستقلا بالفعل لوجب أن يخاف منه كما يخاف من الله تعالى وحينئذ يبطل الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also indicates that a morally responsible person must perform obedience through fear and hope, which are necessary to its validity.
rows.anchor: وفيها دلالة على أنه يجب على المكلف أن يأتي بالطاعات للخوف والرجاء وأن ذلك لا بد منه في صحتها

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some hold that the address to seek help through patience and prayer is to believers in Muhammad, since deniers of prayer and patience in his religion would not be addressed this way.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم : هم المؤمنون بالرسول قال لأن من ينكر الصلاة أصلا والصبر على دين محمد

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: This view allows the discourse to begin by addressing Israelites and then shift to believers in Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ولا يمتنع أن يكون الخطاب أولا في بني إسرائيل ثم يقع بعد ذلك خطابا للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi considers Israelites the likelier audience because assigning the address to another group would disrupt the passage's coherence.
rows.anchor: والأقرب أن المخاطبين هم بنو إسرائيل لأن صرف الخطاب إلى غيرهم يوجب تفكيك النظم

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: An objection asks how Israelites can be ordered to patience and prayer if they reject both.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل كيف يؤمرون بالصبر والصلاة مع كونهم منكرين لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi denies that they rejected the shared meaning: everyone knows patience in what requires patience is good, and prayer humbles one before the Creator and consoles against worldly distress; only its manner differs between Jewish and Muslim prayer.
rows.anchor: لا نسلم كونهم منكرين لهما ؛ وذلك لأن كل أحد يعلم أن الصبر على ما يجب الصبر عليه حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the command concerns the common essence of prayer and patience rather than their differing forms, the objection disappears.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان متعلق الأمر هو الماهية التي هي القدر المشترك زال الإشكال المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ordering faith, abandoning misguidance, and observing laws such as prayer and almsgiving, God prescribes patience and prayer as a remedy because giving up status, wealth, and prestige is difficult.
rows.anchor: لما أمرهم بالإيمان وبترك الإضلال وبالتزام الشرائع وهي الصلاة والزكاة ، وكان ذلك شاقا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes patience as restraining the self from pleasures while accepting Muhammad's religion; habituation makes this easier, and prayer's remembrance of God's majesty, power, mercy, and favor inclines one to obey and avoid sin.
rows.anchor: واستعينوا على ترك ما تحبون من الدنيا والدخول فيما تستثقله طباعكم من قبول دين محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation takes patience to mean fasting: abstaining from food, drink, and sexual desire weakens attachment to worldly life, and with prayer it illuminates the heart with knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: المراد من الصبر ههنا هو الصوم لأن الصائم صابر عن الطعام والشراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting precedes prayer because fasting removes what is undesirable while prayer brings what is desirable, and negation precedes affirmation.
rows.anchor: لأن تأثير الصوم في إزالة ما لا ينبغي وتأثير الصلاة في حصول ما ينبغي والنفي مقدم على الإثبات

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that fasting is a shield against the Fire.
rows.anchor: ولأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال الصوم جنة من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer prevents indecency and wrongdoing, turns one from worldly occupation, humbles the heart, and through recitation and reflection on promises, warnings, and the afterlife makes renouncing worldly leadership easier.
rows.anchor: لأن الصلاة تمنع عن الاشتغال بالدنيا وتخشع القلب ويحصل بسببها تلاوة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parallel command to seek help through patience and prayer appears in the address to believers, with God's support for the patient.
rows.anchor: إن الله مع الصابرين } [ البقرة : 153 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi gives three possible referents for the feminine pronoun: prayer, the implied act of seeking help, or all the commands and prohibitions addressed to Israel from remembering God's favor through this verse.
rows.anchor: أما قوله تعالى { وإنها } ففي هذا الضمير وجوه أحدها : الضمير عائد إلى الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic can omit a noun and refer to it by implication when the hearer understands it; Razi gives examples referring implicitly to earth and a city, as does the verse about God not leaving any creature on it.
rows.anchor: والعرب قد تضمر الشيء اختصارا أو تقتصر فيه على الإيماء إذا وثقت بعلم المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Great means arduous: prayer is hard for those lacking humility but easy for the humble.
rows.anchor: أي لشاقة ثقيلة على هؤلاء سهلة على الخاشعين

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: An objection says this implies the humble bear the greater burden, since they engage their bodies, hearts, hearing, and sight, reflect on their words, and feel grief at warnings and hope at promises.
rows.anchor: وكيف يكون ذلك والخاشع يستعمل عند الصلاة جوارحه وقلبه وسمعه وبصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi clarifies that he does not mean prayer entails more exertion for the humble; it is hard for those who believe in neither reward for doing it nor punishment for leaving it.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد أن الذي يلحقهم من التعب أكثر مما يلحق الخاشع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unbeliever finds prayer burdensome because he sees no benefit, whereas a monotheist expects great benefit from it and harm from neglecting it, so expected reward and escape from punishment make it easier.
rows.anchor: أما الموحد فلما اعتقد في فعلها أعظم المنافع وفي تركها أعظم المضار لم يثقل ذلك عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's difficulty is like bitter medicine: a sick person finds it easy if convinced it will cure him, and difficult without that belief.
rows.anchor: إذا قيل للمريض كل هذا الشيء المر فإن اعتقد أنه له فيه شفاء سهل ذلك عليه

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet described prayer as the coolness of his eyes; Razi says this follows from its benefits, not from prayer being burdensome to him, since he prayed until his feet swelled.
rows.anchor: وجعلت قرة عيني في الصلاة وصف الصلاة بذلك للوجوه التي ذكرناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi defines humility as abasement and submission.
rows.anchor: وأما الخشوع فهو التذلل والخضوع

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The first interpretation takes zann in the phrase about meeting the Lord to mean certain knowledge, since uncertainty about resurrection would be disbelief and cannot be praised.
rows.anchor: أن الظن بمعنى العلم قالوا لأن الظن وهو الإعتقاد الذي يقارنه تجويز النقيض

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: This figurative usage is possible because knowledge and conjecture are both predominant beliefs, although knowledge excludes its opposite while conjecture allows it.
rows.anchor: أن العلم والظن يشتركان في كون كل واحد منهما اعتقادا راجحا

rows.speaker: أوس بن حجر
rows.claim: Aws ibn Hajar's line uses the phrase certain in conjecture as poetic evidence for zann meaning certainty.
rows.anchor: فأرسلته مستيقن الظن أنه … مخالط ما بين الشراسيف خائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an says the speaker in the next life thought he would meet his account, and reproaches those who do not expect resurrection; Razi treats these as evidence for zann meaning knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى { إني ظننت أني ملاق حسابيه } [ الحاقة : 20 ] وقال { ألا يظن أولئك أنهم مبعوثون } [ المطففين : 4 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation retains zann in its ordinary sense of conjecture and offers three explanations of meeting the Lord.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : أن يحمل اللفظ على ظاهره وهو الظن الحقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First, meeting the Lord is a familiar metonym for death, since death causes the meeting; those who expect death at any moment remain humble and hasten to repent.
rows.anchor: الأول : أن تجعل ملاقاة الرب مجازا عن الموت ، وذلك لأن ملاقاة الرب مسبب عن الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of death strengthens the impulse to repent, and a humble person who expects death never assumes that past conduct was free of shortcomings, so must make amends.
rows.anchor: لأن خوف الموت مما يقوي دواعي التوبة مع خشوعه لا بد في كل حال من أن لا يأمن تقصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second, meeting means meeting God's reward, which a worshipful ascetic expects but cannot know with certainty; that expectation produces full humility.
rows.anchor: أن تفسر ملاقاة ثواب الرب وذلك مظنون لا معلوم فإن الزهد العابد لا يقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third, humble people expect to meet God bearing sins because they think poorly of themselves and their deeds, then hurry to repent; this is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: المعنى الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو ربهم بذنوبهم فإن الإنسان الخاشع قد يسيء ظنه بنفسه

rows.speaker: بعض الأصحاب
rows.claim: Some of Razi's associates infer from meeting the Lord that seeing God is possible.
rows.anchor: استدل بعض الأصحاب بقوله { ملاقوا ربهم } على جواز رؤية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites deny that meeting entails seeing, citing verses where meeting means facing hypocrisy, sin, or a threat applying to believers and unbelievers alike.
rows.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : لفظ اللقاء لا يفيد الرؤية والدليل عليه الآية والخبر والعرف

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says one who swears falsely to seize a Muslim's property will meet God while He is angry; Razi says this describes a person of Hell, not a vision of God.
rows.anchor: من حلف على يمين ليقتطع بها مال امرئ مسلم لقي الله وهو عليه غضبان

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Common speech about a person who has died says that he met God, without meaning that he saw God.
rows.anchor: وأما العرف فهو قول المسلمين فيمن مات : لقي الله ، ولا يعنون أنه رأى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They also argue that meeting can mean nearness and removal of a barrier, as when someone says he has not met a prince despite seeing him, or says he met him when admitted, even if blind.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فاللقاء يراد به القرب ممن يلقاه على زجه يزول الحجاب بينهما

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Other ordinary uses mean encountering hardship, calamity, or death, which further show that meeting does not itself mean seeing.
rows.anchor: ويقال لقي فلان جهدا شديدا ولقيت من فلان الداهية ، ولاقى فلان حمامه

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They cite the waters meeting as a physical encounter, a meaning that cannot apply to God, as evidence that meeting is not synonymous with vision.
rows.anchor: فالتقى الماء على أمر قد قدر } [ القمر : 12 ] وهذا إنما يصح في حق الجسم ولا يصح على الله تعالى
